title: The MiniMax-M2 Series: Mini Activations Unleashing Max Real-World Intelligence
data_curation: Pretraining uses 29.2T tokens (19.9T in the constant phase plus a 9.3T decay phase), with quality scored by reward models and classifiers and with code, math and STEM upsampled. Post-training data comes from agent-driven pipelines, each tied to an executable workspace and a reward matched to the artifact. SWE scaling crawls permissively licensed GitHub PRs and agent-builds Docker environments for 10+ languages. It routes each PR by type to a reward (F2P/P2P tests for bug fixes, new test points for features, stable perf deltas for optimizations), checks problem/test consistency with an LLM, and augments by bug injection, commit merging, SWE-Test inversion and code review. AppDev combines expert meta-queries, MinHash dedup, rubric filtering, prompt distillation and Agent-as-a-Verifier rejection sampling (execution, Playwright interaction and visual-aesthetics layers). Terminal-Gym turns Stack Overflow posts into verified Docker tasks with hint removal and difficulty calibration. Cowork data covers deep search (guide-and-rewrite obfuscation, evidence-grounded acceptance), GDPval-anchored office tasks, finance and spreadsheets (value-level recalculation match) and slides (a rendered visual scorer).
curriculum: Pretraining extends context from 8K to 32K to 192K, mixing high-quality and long-context data (code concatenation, long PDFs, document packing) into the decay phase. During the decay phase MTP grows from 1 to 3 modules by weight copying: the MTP heads first train with the main model frozen, then everything trains jointly. Post-training runs interleaved-thinking SFT (chat, reasoning, code and cowork, built by rejection sampling) as the cold start, followed by multi-stage mixed-domain RL. Every RL stage draws reasoning, coding, agent and general data together. Across stages the mix shifts from reasoning/general toward agent/coding, the context length grows per domain, and difficulty moves toward harder tasks; this is chosen to avoid both forgetting and negative transfer between domains. The series iterates M2 to M2.5 to M2.7.
method: M2 is a 62-layer MoE with 229.9B total and 9.8B active parameters: 256 fine-grained experts with top-8 sigmoid gating and learnable expert bias, full GQA attention (48 query heads, 8 KV heads), RoPE, a 200,064-token vocabulary, and MTP used for speculative decoding. The authors chose full attention after hybrid SWA variants lost accuracy beyond 32K context. RL uses CISPO: token-level loss normalized by total tokens, with a stop-gradient on the IS weight clipped to [0, 1+eps_high]. Advantages are reward-to-go minus a trajectory baseline. Each training sample is an (s_t, a_t) pair, so context management counts as part of the environment. The composite reward adds process rewards (penalties for language mixing and tool-format errors), a completion-time reward against a baseline, and the outcome reward. The Forge system decouples the agent side, a Gateway/Data Pool middleware layer, and the rollout/train engines, which lets it train white-box and black-box agents. Forge adds windowed-FIFO scheduling (W=0.3N), prefix-tree merging (up to 40x training speedup), MTP heads co-trained with top-K KL, prefill-decode disaggregation and a global L3 KV cache. The model keeps its thinking across turns (interleaved thinking).
eval_metrics: Coding benchmarks are SWE-bench Pro, SWE-bench Multilingual, Multi-SWE-bench, internal NL2Repo (all on a Claude Code scaffold, 4 trials), Terminal-Bench 2.0 (Terminus-2) and MLE Bench Lite (medal rate, 3x24h). AppDev uses internal VIBE-Pro and HyperTask. Search uses BrowseComp, Wide Search and internal RISE. Office and tools use GDPval-AA, Toolathlon, internal MM Claw, MEWC v2 and Finance Modeling Pro. Reasoning uses AIME 2026, GPQA-D, SciCode, IFBench, AA-LCR, HLE and MMLU-Pro under the AA Index v4.0 protocol (pass@1). M2.7 scores: SWE-bench Pro 56.2, SWE-Multilingual 76.5, Multi-SWE 52.7, Terminal-Bench 2.0 57.0, MLE Lite 66.6, VIBE-Pro 55.6, BrowseComp 77.8, GDPval-AA 50.0, Toolathlon 46.3, AIME26 94.2, GPQA-D 89.8, IFBench 76.0, HLE 28.0.
key_results: With about 10B active parameters, M2.7 is close to closed frontier models. It has the best Multi-SWE-bench score among the compared models (52.7 vs 50.3 for Opus 4.6), scores 56.2 on SWE-bench Pro against 57.3 for Opus 4.6 and 57.7 for GPT 5.4, and reaches a 66.6% MLE Bench Lite medal rate, tying Gemini 3.1 Pro. From M2 to M2.7 every tracked benchmark improves, for example BrowseComp by 33.8 points and Toolathlon by 27.5. M2.7 also handles 30-50% of the RL team's daily iteration work and, in 100 autonomous rounds of improving an internal scaffold, gained 30%.
evolution_note: The series follows MiniMax-01 and MiniMax-M1 and keeps M1's CISPO objective, but it drops their hybrid Lightning Attention in favour of full attention, after SWA hybrids degraded on agent tasks longer than 32K. It borrows MTP and auxiliary-loss-free expert-bias routing from DeepSeek-V3 and SWE-Smith-style task augmentation. It moves post-training from reasoning RL toward agent-native RL over arbitrary black-box scaffolds, and it gives an early, partly human-steered example of a model debugging its own training runs. Note: the arXiv ID is 2605 (May 2026, v2 dated July 2026), earlier than the corpus's 2608-2610 target window.
